article_title: “When I Think of Black Girls, I Think of Opportunities”: Black Girls' Identity Development and the Protective Role of Parental Socialization in Educational Settings
citation: Burnett Marketa, McBride Margarett, Green McKenzie N., Cooper Shauna M. (2022). “When I Think of Black Girls, I Think of Opportunities”: Black Girls' Identity Development and the Protective Role of Parental Socialization in Educational Settings. Frontiers in Psychology. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2022.933476
title: Phenomenological Variant of Ecological Systems Theory (PVEST)
description: PVEST is Spencer's model of how Black children process and make meaning of lived experiences. It begins with self-other appraisals—perceptions of how others view one, with attention to biases and stereotypes—and "PVEST posits that how someone makes meaning of these self-other appraisals also impacts their stress engagement which leads to their reactive coping strategies." Stable identities emerge through adaptive or maladaptive coping, leading to adverse or productive outcomes. The study used PVEST as its guiding framework for a theoretical thematic analysis of girls' meaning-making.
requirements: Codes and analysis aligned with PVEST and the research questions, emphasizing youths' own meaning-making as interpreters of their experiences
target_learners: adolescent Black girls in middle school and high school
target_learning_goals: coping with gendered racism in educational settings
examples: The study's codebook of seven overarching identity and socialization codes was developed to closely align with PVEST and the research questions
key_sources: Burnett Marketa, McBride Margarett, Green McKenzie N., Cooper Shauna M. (2022). “When I Think of Black Girls, I Think of Opportunities”: Black Girls' Identity Development and the Protective Role of Parental Socialization in Educational Settings. Frontiers in Psychology. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2022.933476

article_title: A Longitudinal Examination of Racial Identity and Racial Discrimination Among African American Adolescents
citation: Seaton Eleanor K., Yip Tiffany, Sellers Robert M. (2009). A Longitudinal Examination of Racial Identity and Racial Discrimination Among African American Adolescents. Child Development. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8624.2009.01268.x
title: PVEST: racial discrimination as a chronic stressor around which emergent identities are formed through coping
description: The Phenomenological Variant of Ecological Systems Theory incorporates ecological systems with identity development for minority youth. The article states PVEST "argues that racial discrimination is a risk factor, which increases the net vulnerability for youth of color", and that "emergent identities arise out of coping with stressors like racial discrimination". The authors report their public regard findings support a PVEST tenet that it should not be assumed African American youth form negative identities in the context of racial discrimination.
requirements: Identity development is considered central and foundational, providing the foundation for future productive or adverse behavior
constraints: The framework was tested here only for identity content dimensions (centrality, regard), not identity development processes such as exploration
target_learners: Minority youth, specifically African American adolescents
target_learning_goals: Understanding identity development as coping with racial discrimination as a chronic stressor
examples: The authors state the decreasing public regard levels and discrimination-to-public-regard link are consistent with PVEST's person-context process
key_sources: Seaton Eleanor K., Yip Tiffany, Sellers Robert M. (2009). A Longitudinal Examination of Racial Identity and Racial Discrimination Among African American Adolescents. Child Development. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8624.2009.01268.x

article_title: The effect of three different techniques used to improve vein prominence on the first peripheral venous catheterization experience in nursing students: a randomized controlled study.
citation: Yılmaz Hülya, Yılmaz Dilek, Çinar Hava Gökdere. (2025). The effect of three different techniques used to improve vein prominence on the first peripheral venous catheterization experience in nursing students: a randomized controlled study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07350-0
title: PVC assessment instrument set: five-step vein prominence scale, PVC-KEF knowledge form, and C-PVC 20-step checklist
description: The study used three instruments: a five-step vein prominence scale ("1 = no veins visible or palpable... 5 = clearly visible and easily palpable veins"); the PVC Knowledge Evaluation Form (PVC-KEF) of 20 questions scored 0–100, with a content validity index of 0.98 after review by five nursing and five measurement-evaluation experts; and the Checklist for PVC (C-PVC) covering 20 procedure steps scored 0–2 each (0–40 total), with a content validity index of 1.0 and inter-rater ICC of 0.899 between two independent researchers.
requirements: Expert content-validity review and pilot comprehension testing with third-year nursing students before use
constraints: The authors state more testing in broader contexts and populations is required to improve the instruments' applicability
target_learning_goals: assessing PVC knowledge, psychomotor skill performance, and vein prominence
examples: Two independent researchers scored psychomotor performance with the C-PVC checklist while a chronometer recorded procedure duration from tourniquet application to steel-needle removal
key_sources: Yılmaz Hülya, Yılmaz Dilek, Çinar Hava Gökdere. (2025). The effect of three different techniques used to improve vein prominence on the first peripheral venous catheterization experience in nursing students: a randomized controlled study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07350-0

article_title: The effects of personalized video feedback of basic cardiac life support on knowledge and skills levels in undergraduate nursing students: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Mohsenzadeh Habibeh, Farsi Zahra, Afaghi Effat. (2025). The effects of personalized video feedback of basic cardiac life support on knowledge and skills levels in undergraduate nursing students: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06935-z
title: Provide personalized video feedback alongside simulation-based training to sustain and improve clinical skills over time
description: The article recommends giving students a recording of their own practice with detailed personalized feedback on strengths, weaknesses, mistakes, and corrections, in addition to immediate face-to-face feedback. In the trial, students "could watch the video as many times as they needed to progress in their learning process and master CPCR," and the authors recommend the method "due to its self-directed and universal orientation and special attention to the individual differences of students."
requirements: Training must include lecture and simulation-based practice on a mannequin, with the student's performance recorded and individualized feedback recorded onto the video.
Students must have access to their own personalized video after training.
constraints: Evidence comes from a single trial of 40 female first-year nursing students at one nursing school; the authors note a chance of contamination bias between groups and recommend further studies in larger groups and both genders.
target_learning_goals: basic cardiac life support knowledge and skills
clinical procedure skills requiring bedside application
examples: After practicing BCLS on a simulated mannequin in groups of seven, each student's performance was recorded with a digital camera, the researcher recorded feedback on strengths, weaknesses, mistakes, and corrections, and the video was given to experimental-group students.
key_sources: Mohsenzadeh Habibeh, Farsi Zahra, Afaghi Effat. (2025). The effects of personalized video feedback of basic cardiac life support on knowledge and skills levels in undergraduate nursing students: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06935-z

article_title: Mastery learning improves students skills in inserting intravenous access: a pre-post-study.
citation: Friederichs Hendrik, Brouwer Britta, Marschall Bernhard, Weissenstein Anne. (2016). Mastery learning improves students skills in inserting intravenous access: a pre-post-study. GMS Journal for Medical Education. http://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2016-33/zma001055.shtml
title: 21-point PVC insertion checklist with Hofstee-set pass mark of 20
description: The measuring instrument is a checklist divided into four units — preparing materials, preparation of the puncture, execution of the puncture, and fixation of the venous catheter — with seven, four, five and five subunits respectively, each successfully performed sub-unit scoring one point for a total of 21 points. The structure follows the OSCE checklist of Juenger and Nikendei. "a Hofstee score of 20 points was used as the final minimum passing score", set by a multidisciplinary panel of eight clinical experts, so passing required correct skin disinfection.
requirements: a multidisciplinary expert panel trained in standard setting to determine the minimum passing score
trained peer tutors schooled on the checklist for about one hour
constraints: the pass mark was defined as 20 of 21 for reasons of patient safety, making it impossible to pass without correctly disinfecting the skin
target_learning_goals: correct peripheral venous catheter insertion including hygiene steps
examples: Subunits included retrieving gloves, disinfection of the puncture site and announcing the puncture to the patient.
key_sources: Friederichs Hendrik, Brouwer Britta, Marschall Bernhard, Weissenstein Anne. (2016). Mastery learning improves students skills in inserting intravenous access: a pre-post-study. GMS Journal for Medical Education. http://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2016-33/zma001055.shtml
